alerts.subject: CMA CGM and Maersk not queried this run
alerts.detail: Deliberate. The CMA routing-finder DataDome quota is shared with the liner-tracker-market-refresh task on the same IP, and Maersk requires a UI-seeded header capture. Every code either would have returned was captured elsewhere: Ocean Alliance via Evergreen, Gemini via the Hapag-Lloyd public API. This is a self-imposed gap, not a block.

alerts.subject: AUG promoted to serviceRegistry - not an extra loader
alerts.detail: AUG surfaced as an unknown code with n=2 on CNYTN-USHOU via Evergreen (CONTI CORTESIA 014E 11 Sep, ONE HUMEN 101E 08 Sep). Vessel drill-down returns the verbatim label 'Asia-U.S. GULF Service(AUG)' with a fixed round-trip rotation and consecutive voyage numbers 013E/013W/014E/014W. ONE Route Finder returns the SAME two vessels and voyage numbers under EC4. AUG is Evergreen's name for the Premier Alliance Gulf string. Added to Premier Alliance in the registry with alias AUG=EC4. Flagged under this alert type because n=2 rather than the n>=3 threshold; it is a registry gap, not a discovery.

alerts.subject: NSB, KTH and FP2 added to ignoredCodes
alerts.detail: NSB and KTH appeared on KRPUS-USNYC via Evergreen with southbound 'S' voyage suffixes and 42-49 day transits: these are intra-Asia feeder legs captured as the first leg of a transshipment routing, not USEC services. FP2 appeared the same way on ONE CNYTN-USNYC (Transshipment rows). All three denied at parse time from now on.
